name: Shipping Corporation of India Ltd
tagline: India's largest PSU shipping company, cheap on P/E and mid-way through a large fleet-modernization program, but a stalled privatization and a decade of poor sales growth keep this a large-cap value/cyclical play, not a growth thesis.
business_overview: SCI operates a diversified fleet (crude/product tankers, LPG carriers, bulk carriers, container ships, passenger vessels; 55+ vessels, 3.5m+ DWT) as India's largest government-owned shipping company. It has announced a ~$2.3bn domestic newbuild program (26 ships, ~1.18m GT, phased delivery) to modernize the fleet with dual-fuel (LNG-capable) vessels ahead of IMO 2030 carbon-intensity rules. Long-pending privatization appears stalled again - recent reports suggest the government may pause disinvestment given global shipping-route disruptions and a strategic desire to retain a state-owned fleet. Seeded 2026-09-13 via untrusted X triage (@r_laroia, high conviction).
fundamentals_table: 5-year sales growth ~9.31% - described by screener as poor
fundamentals_narrative: Cheap (P/E ~8.3x, decent ROE ~15%) but this is a commodity freight-rate business with a mediocre 9.31% 5-year sales growth track record. The one specific, named structural item found this pass is the ~$2.3bn/26-ship domestic newbuild and fleet-modernization program (dual-fuel, IMO-2030-compliant) - a genuine capacity/quality upgrade, but phased over several years and dependent on global tanker/bulk/LNG rate cycles playing out favourably. The long-running privatization story, which would have been the cleanest re-rating catalyst, appears to be paused again rather than progressing.
